title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
before: Language was studied as grammar and meaning, not as a measurable signal.
problem: No way to quantify how predictable a stretch of text is.
breakthrough: Entropy, and the idea that a text source can be modelled as a probability distribution over the next symbol.
why: Every language model since scores itself on how surprised it is by the next token. That is Shannon's measure.
next: Statistical speech recognition and machine translation at IBM through the 1970s-80s.
inherits: Cross-entropy loss, perplexity, and the framing of language as prediction.
